ownership_reason: Only the gold turns the offset text of a GMT display name into a zone; hops 1-4 resolve the ID UTC, place the provider, look the ID up and select the offset text, and once the offset reaches the gold no caller receives anything but the gold's zone. The variant gold never returns the DateTimeZone.UTC instance for any input (it always constructs a new FixedDateTimeZone), so no change of what hops 1-4 pass to it makes the trigger pass; an edit outside the gold passes only by producing UTC itself or by re-resolving the result (bypasses). The convention is pinned outside the gold: in this code base the DateTimeZone object for a zero offset is DateTimeZone.UTC and no factory produces a zone with the ID +00:00. DateTimeZone.forID returns UTC for a zero +hh:mm offset (testForID_String: assertSame(UTC, forID("+00:00")) and forID("+00")), DateTimeZone.forOffsetMillis returns UTC for 0 through fixedOffsetZone (testForOffsetMillis_int: assertSame(UTC, forOffsetMillis(0))), and DateTimeZone.forOffsetHoursMinutes returns UTC for (0, 0) (testForOffsetHoursMinutes_int_int). The gold's javadoc is the house contract of forOffsetMillis ('a time zone instance for the specified offset', 'the DateTimeZone object for the offset'), which a FixedDateTimeZone with the ID +00:00, not equal to UTC, violates for a zero offset. testTimeZoneConversion pins the non-zero GMT display-name path (GMT-10:00 gives -10:00) and passes on the variant.
